title: GPS-BLOCK: signed-leaf multibit decoding with polynomial workspace

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-BLOCK algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (width profile Delta=2ceil(log2(4R)), per-node success at least 1/2 with r=b+1 inputs, G=2^m q0, Wstar=2m2^R H0, signed-leaf multibit odd decoder, root-frequency guard, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and weighted-attempt cutoff Wcap and capped verified-extraction fallback Cf) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, its total charged sequential work obeys T(N,s) = O(n^(5/2) (log2 n)^(3/2) 2^((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n))). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_T(n) = n^(5/2) (log2 n)^(3/2) 2^((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n)) for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases; the inner coefficient 176777/250000 is established by the explicit bound R(n) <= ceil((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n)), where R(n) is the profile parameter of proof.md Section 4.1 (the least integer R >= 2 with S(R) >= n - 1), proved for all n >= 2^16777216 by the threshold Lemma 9.2 and Corollary 9.2' of proof.md, the finitely many smaller bit lengths being covered by the absolute outer constant. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-BLOCK algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (width profile, signed-leaf multibit odd decoder, root-frequency guard, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and weighted-attempt cutoff Wcap and capped verified-extraction fallback Cf) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, its peak allocated classical bits obey S_C(N,s) = O(n^2). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_C(n) = n^2 for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, its peak allocated qubits obey S_Q(N,s) = O(n). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_Q(n) = n for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases. Its exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For every integer N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single GPS-BLOCK algorithm and complete parameter rule of proof.md (width profile, signed-leaf multibit odd decoder, root-frequency guard, Grover pair search, acquisition cutoff Qcap and weighted-attempt cutoff Wcap and capped verified-extraction fallback Cf) recovers the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 from independent ideal source copies. On EVERY execution branch, including all retries, discarded copies, failed attempts and aborts, the total number of fresh DCP source copies acquired, counting every rejected, discarded and failed copy, obeys Q(N,s) = O(2^((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n))). The uniform bit-length envelope is B_samples(n) = 2^((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n)) for n >= 2, with the explicit finite branch covering all smaller cases; the inner coefficient 176777/250000 is established by the explicit bound R(n) <= ceil((176777/250000) sqrt(n log2 n)), where R(n) is the profile parameter of proof.md Section 4.1 (the least integer R >= 2 with S(R) >= n - 1), proved for all n >= 2^16777216 by the threshold Lemma 9.2 and Corollary 9.2' of proof.md, the finitely many smaller bit lengths being covered by the absolute outer constant. Its exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes, and this bound holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the zero-tolerance claim for this same algorithm/configuration.

For the same GPS-BLOCK algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8 > 3/4 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
